subject: general
question: As of July 2022, students from how many minority communities under the Maulana Azad Fellowship Scheme (MANF) get five year fellowships in the form of financial assistance notified by the Central Government, to pursue M. Phil and Ph.D?
solution:
The correct answer is __**six.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Students from six minority communities under the Maulana Azad Fellowship Scheme (MANF) get five-year fellowships in the form of financial assistance notified by the Central Government, to pursue M. Phil and Ph.D.**
 
• The minority communities are **Buddhist, Christian, Jain, Muslim, Parsi and Sikh**.
 
• The MANF scheme was launched by the Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India, in 2003 to provide financial assistance to students from minority communities to pursue higher education.
 
• **The scheme aims to provide opportunities to minority students to undertake advanced studies and research in science, humanities, social sciences, and engineering and technology.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **The Maulana Azad Fellowship Scheme (MANF) is named after Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, who was an Indian scholar and the first education minister of independent India.**
 
• The MANF scheme is implemented through the **University Grants Commission (UGC)**, which is the apex body for higher education in India.
 
• The MANF scheme provides financial assistance to students from minority communities to pursue M. Phil and Ph.D. in universities, deemed universities, and research institutions recognized by the UGC.
 
• **The MANF scheme provides financial assistance in the form of a monthly stipend, contingency grant, and other benefits.**
 
• The scheme also provides a separate ad-hoc grant to the universities and institutions to provide infrastructure and other facilities to the MANF scholars.
